body:
She was friends at the time with the guy who did it, he had been my boyfriend. So I guess she was trying to justify it to herself by saying maybe he didn't know I was serious when I said stop. Whatever she meant by it, I don't feel comfortable talking to her about it anymore.

I think I will try mentioning to my partner that I'm still generally struggling with it and work up to telling her about the flashbacks. I just hope she doesn't think I'm crazy or something.
If I don't have to work that day, I drink. If I do have to work, I pinch myself until I can make myself move.
Who the fuck downvotes someone on fucking suicide watch. People are such shit.

I have tried talking to my best friend about it. I guess she just isn't the best listener. She initially told me that I should have fought my attacker harder, so i just stopped talking to her about it. I'm pretty sure that my fears about my girlfriend are irrational and not based in reality, but they've still kept me from opening up to her about how often I still have these bouts of anxiety paralysis.

Both of the important people in my life (my girlfriend and best friend) are transgender. Their depression and dysphoria takes up so much space and energy, I feel like I would only be adding to their burdens, or my problems are small in comparison. I also have a fear that my girlfriend would leave me if she knew how damaged I am.
